summary: Scheduled 60-second public-information probes consumed the deployed release's default 1000/day quotas for the root and metadata endpoints, making quota exhaustion visible to traffic sharing an exhausted application-visible identity.
impact: The public landing page and metadata endpoint returned HTTP 429 to affected traffic, while the relay remained healthy and health, version, and compute polling requests continued succeeding in retained evidence.
fix: Mitigated. Production Helm revision 7 deployed ghcr.io/futuroptimist/tokenplace-relay:sha-6c39adc (OCI index sha256:543fde33aff45253630090b52d16163e3586da12c973f5c4a658ddc8927d0a68, source 6c39adc64e7bed4f85d07164aa2860e637919ca9, version 0.1.1). Root and /api/v1/meta probes were restored alongside /livez and /healthz; each restored target had three successful samples and min_over_time(probe_success[3m])=1. The initial restoration soak had zero 429s or 5xx responses, compute polls increased from 222 to 260, memory remained 65,101,824-65,425,408 bytes of 268,435,456, and authenticated application scraping was restored at 227 bounded samples. No monitoring remains intentionally disabled, but a full 24-hour quota window or direct quota-counter evidence is still required; all action items remain open.
lessons: Release parity must preserve reviewed safety fixes; synthetic request frequency must be validated against endpoint quotas, quota pressure needs privacy-safe early warning, and process replacement is a risky reset rather than a permanent correction.
